policy.no_fabrication: Every row must cite a source that already exists in this repository or is supplied by a completed source-grounded research pass. Unknown fields are recorded as the string 'unknown' or an empty list, never guessed.
policy.no_causal_claims: Rows describe risk-associated features, early-development signals or biological pathways. A causal claim requires a source whose study design supports causal inference and must set marker_class or limitations accordingly.
policy.no_universal_marker_claim: The catalogue must not assert that a cancer has no specific biomarker. Site-specific markers exist; the defensible statement is that no single marker is universally sufficient for early detection, so panels and interacting features are required.
policy.doctor_facing_gate: A row may only be surfaced in a clinician-facing view when primary_source_url is a real URL and evidence_grade is not 'unknown'.
policy.seed_provenance: Rows 1-8 are transcribed from docs/RESEARCH_EVIDENCE.md section 2 (candidate metabolic biomarkers) and section 1, which were compiled with source links inside this repository. No new literature was introduced.
policy.placeholders: Two explicit placeholders are allowed and are never inferred: 'unknown' means the value exists but was not extracted from the source, and 'n.a.' means the field does not apply to this row. Empty strings are a validation error.
policy.statement_gate: allowlisted_statements may only be used verbatim-in-substance when the row is clinician-ready (real source URL or DOI plus a graded evidence level). denied_statements must never be said, written or displayed.

entries.stage_or_lead_time: Strongest within 2 years of diabetes diagnosis; attenuates with longer follow-up
entries.performance: OR 2.42 (1.33-4.39) highest vs lowest category; OR 3.41 within 2 years of diabetes diagnosis; OR 1.45 with longer follow-up
entries.limitations: Association with prevalent/incident cancer in a diabetes context, not a stand-alone early-detection test. No lead-time-specific operating point.

entries.performance: OR 4.24 (1.30-13.8, p-trend<0.001) highest vs lowest quartile; fasting insulin showed no association
entries.limitations: Wide confidence interval. Nonfasting measurement; fasting insulin null in the same study. Not an early-detection operating point.

entries.performance: T2D >5 years duration RR 1.5-2x; insulin resistance without diagnosed diabetes reported with 33% attributable risk for pancreatic cancer mortality
entries.limitations: Review-level synthesis; attributable-risk figure is mortality-based, not incidence, and not an individual-level test characteristic.

entries.stage_or_lead_time: Sensitivity 68% at 1 year pre-diagnosis, 53% at 2 years (95% specificity); exponential rise begins about 2 years before diagnosis; AUC 0.87 in the 0-6 month pre-diagnosis window
entries.performance: See stage_or_lead_time; performance is strongly lead-time dependent
entries.limitations: This is the clearest counter-example to the idea that no cancer has a specific marker, but it is NOT a universal early-detection solution: sensitivity falls sharply with lead time and it is not measured in NHANES, so it cannot be used in this project's current data.

entries.performance: OR 77.82 (p<0.001) for >=10% loss vs stable weight; OR 10.30 for 5-10% loss; 74.9% of PDAC patients lost >=5% in the year before diagnosis vs 11.2% of controls
entries.limitations: Case-control design with recall and reverse-causation concerns: weight loss close to diagnosis may be an effect of the tumour rather than an early independent signal. Effect sizes this large are design-inflated.

entries.performance: BMI>=30 vs 21-22.9 RR 1.47 (1.23-1.75); waist-to-hip ratio highest vs lowest quartile RR 1.35 (1.03-1.78)
entries.limitations: Population-level relative risks with small absolute effect; not usable as an individual early-detection signal.

entries.performance: Continuous OR 0.98 (0.95-1.01), not significant; direction inconsistent between cohorts
entries.limitations: Explicit negative result. Any hs-CRP-based feature must be documented as a known-weak predictor rather than assumed informative.

entries.performance: unknown
entries.limitations: Declared evidence gap in this repository: no usable quantitative data was retrieved. Lipid features may be modelled but must not be described as evidence-supported.

entries.marker_or_panel: New-onset-diabetes clinical risk panels (ENDPAC; QResearch Cox model)
entries.sample_size: ENDPAC validation 107305 NOD patients (48 cases / 6254 controls analytic); QResearch 253766 new T2DM diagnoses with 767 pancreatic cancer cases within 2 years
entries.performance: ENDPAC AUC 0.72, sensitivity 56% / specificity 75% at the recommended cutoff, prevalence enriched 0.78% -> 1.7%; QResearch C-index 0.802 (0.787-0.817), calibration slope 0.980, top 1% of predicted risk captured 12.51% of cases
entries.limitations: Panels, not single markers, and restricted to new-onset-diabetes populations. These are the realistic performance ceiling for comparison; they are not reproduced in this project and cannot be with cross-sectional data.

entries.marker_or_panel: Genetic + clinical new-onset-diabetes pancreatic cancer model
entries.performance: unknown
entries.limitations: Cited in this repository as a design reference. Quantitative fields deliberately left unknown until a source-grounded pass extracts them; do not quote performance from this row.

entries.marker_or_panel: Clinical CatBoost model with multi-omics integration
entries.performance: unknown
entries.limitations: Cited in this repository as a modelling reference. Quantitative fields deliberately left unknown until a source-grounded pass extracts them.

entries.stage_or_lead_time: Prediagnostic performance decays steeply with lead time: AUC 0.998 at diagnosis, 0.87 at 6 months, 0.74 at 12 months, 0.55 at 5 years before diagnosis
entries.performance: AUC 0.998 at diagnosis; 0.87 at 6 months; 0.74 at 12 months; 0.55 at 5 years prediagnostic
entries.limitations: Not recommended for screening asymptomatic adults; the USPSTF recommends against screening for pancreatic cancer in asymptomatic adults. Discrimination at 12 months and beyond is weak to near-chance, so the strong at-diagnosis AUC must never be quoted as early-detection performance. CA19-9 is not measured in NHANES, so it cannot be used in this project's current data.
allowlisted_statements: A pancreas-specific marker exists (CA19-9), but its discrimination falls from near-perfect at diagnosis to about 0.74 at 12 months and 0.55 at 5 years before diagnosis.
CA19-9 is not recommended for screening asymptomatic adults.
denied_statements: CA19-9 detects pancreatic cancer early.
No cancer has a specific biomarker.
An AUC of 0.998 shows CA19-9 works for screening.
entries.notes: Primary counter-example to any claim that site-specific markers do not exist.

entries.performance: c-statistic 0.97; 87% sensitivity at 98% specificity
entries.limitations: Clinically detected cases versus controls only, with no prediagnostic specimens, so the reported accuracy is spectrum-biased and says nothing about early detection. Neither marker is available in this project's data.
allowlisted_statements: A two-marker plasma panel reached a c-statistic of 0.97 in a case-control discovery study of 537 samples.
This panel has no prediagnostic lead-time evidence, so it is a discovery result rather than an early-detection result.
denied_statements: THBS2 plus CA19-9 detects pancreatic cancer before symptoms.
A c-statistic of 0.97 means this panel is ready for clinical screening.

entries.marker_or_panel: CA19-9 + CA125 + VWF + THBS2 + IL6ST (five-marker plasma panel)
entries.stage_or_lead_time: AUC 0.91 within 1 year of diagnosis; 0.78 up to 4 years before diagnosis
entries.performance: AUC 0.91 within 1 year; AUC 0.78 up to 4 years prediagnostic
entries.limitations: Internal/discovery evaluation with no external validation; the individual study sample size could not be confirmed from the available source and is recorded as unknown rather than estimated. None of the five markers is measured in NHANES.
allowlisted_statements: A five-marker plasma panel reported AUC 0.91 within one year of diagnosis and 0.78 up to four years before diagnosis, in internal discovery evaluation only.
Panels outperform single markers at longer lead times in this evidence, which is why early detection is treated as a panel problem.
denied_statements: This panel is validated for pancreatic cancer screening.
An AUC of 0.78 four years out means we can detect pancreatic cancer four years early in practice.

entries.marker_or_panel: ENDPAC score (age, change in glucose, change in weight)
entries.stage_or_lead_time: Within the new-onset-diabetes window used by the score
entries.performance: AUC 0.75; high-risk stratum PPV 2.0%; NPV 99.7%
entries.limitations: Risk stratification within new-onset diabetes, not a detection test: a 2.0% PPV means 98 of 100 flagged patients do not have pancreatic cancer. Restricted to new-onset-diabetes populations, which the current cross-sectional data cannot identify because there is no follow-up time.
allowlisted_statements: ENDPAC uses age, glucose change and weight change to stratify risk within new-onset diabetes, with AUC 0.75 and a high-risk PPV of 2.0%.
Published risk-stratification panels in this space reach AUCs around 0.75, which is the realistic comparison point for our work.
denied_statements: ENDPAC detects pancreatic cancer.
A high ENDPAC score means the patient has pancreatic cancer.
entries.notes: Separate source and cohort from ev-nod-panc-benchmark-models; both rows are kept because they report different validations of the same score family.

entries.marker_or_panel: Recent-onset diabetes (<=4 years) combined with >8 lb weight loss
entries.stage_or_lead_time: Within the 4-year window after diabetes onset
entries.performance: Incidence ratio 10.57 (95% CI 7.18-15.56) versus no recent diabetes and no weight loss; absolute 4-year incidence 0.29%
entries.limitations: A 10-fold relative increase still corresponds to a 0.29% absolute 4-year incidence, so this combination cannot function as a stand-alone detection rule. Association only; reverse causation is plausible because both diabetes and weight loss can be consequences of an occult tumour.
allowlisted_statements: Recent-onset diabetes combined with weight loss carries an incidence ratio of 10.57, yet the absolute 4-year incidence is only 0.29%.
This is why a strong relative association is not the same as a usable detection rule.
denied_statements: Recent diabetes plus weight loss means the patient probably has pancreatic cancer.
Diabetes causes pancreatic cancer.
entries.notes: The interacting-feature pattern this study describes is the kind of interaction the current cross-sectional data cannot evaluate, because diabetes onset timing and subsequent incidence are both unavailable.

entries.stage_or_lead_time: Within 1 year of the raised platelet count
entries.performance: 1-year cancer PPV 11.6% in men and 6.2% in women; after a second raised count 18.1% and 10.1%; cancers were mainly lung and colorectal
entries.limitations: Non-specific risk marker across sites, not a site-assigning or diagnostic test. Derived from primary-care records with possible investigation bias. Platelet count is present in this project's data, but no incident-cancer follow-up exists to reproduce anything like this analysis.
allowlisted_statements: A raised platelet count carries a 1-year cancer positive predictive value of 11.6% in men and 6.2% in women, rising to 18.1% and 10.1% after a second raised count.
Thrombocytosis is a non-specific risk marker across cancer sites, mainly lung and colorectal, and does not indicate which site is involved.
denied_statements: A high platelet count indicates pancreatic cancer.
Thrombocytosis is an early-detection test for cancer.

entries.performance: Sufficient evidence for cancers of the colon, kidney, postmenopausal breast, corpus uteri, liver, pancreas and ovary
entries.limitations: A risk association across multiple sites, not an early-detection signal and not a site-specific marker. The human causal effect of intentional weight loss on cancer incidence remains unestablished, so no intervention claim follows.
allowlisted_statements: IARC found sufficient evidence linking excess body fatness to cancers of the colon, kidney, postmenopausal breast, corpus uteri, liver, pancreas and ovary.
The human causal effect of intentional weight loss on cancer incidence remains unestablished.
denied_statements: Losing weight prevents cancer.
Obesity causes pancreatic cancer in this patient.
BMI can be used to detect cancer early.

entries.marker_or_panel: GALAD score (sex, age, AFP-L3, AFP, DCP)
entries.performance: AUC 0.78 within 12 months versus 0.66 for AFP alone; 62% sensitivity at 82% specificity
entries.limitations: Applies only to surveillance of high-risk patients with cirrhosis, not to population screening, and not to pancreatic cancer. Sensitivity of 62% means a substantial share of cancers is missed. None of its markers exists in this project's data.
allowlisted_statements: GALAD is a five-component panel for surveillance of high-risk cirrhosis that reached AUC 0.78 within 12 months of diagnosis, against 0.66 for AFP alone, with 62% sensitivity at 82% specificity.
This is the clearest example that a validated panel outperforms a single marker, and that it works in a defined high-risk population rather than the general population.
denied_statements: GALAD can screen the general population for liver cancer.
A GALAD-style approach would work for pancreatic cancer in NHANES.

entries.marker_or_panel: CancerSEEK (protein markers plus cell-free DNA mutations)
entries.performance: Median sensitivity 70% at specificity above 99%; stage I sensitivity 43%; breast cancer sensitivity 33%
entries.limitations: Clinically detected cases only, so there is no prediagnostic lead time and the cohort is spectrum-biased for screening use. Stage I sensitivity of 43% is the figure that matters for early detection, not the 70% median. Not reproducible in this project: no cell-free DNA or protein panel exists in the current data.
allowlisted_statements: A multi-analyte blood test reported 70% median sensitivity at over 99% specificity in a case-control study, but only 43% sensitivity at stage I and 33% for breast cancer.
Because the cases were clinically detected, this evidence carries no prediagnostic lead time and is spectrum-biased for screening.
denied_statements: A single blood test can already detect any cancer early.
70% sensitivity means CancerSEEK finds most cancers early.

claims_contract.purpose: Reporting and design standards that any MetaboGuard claim about detection performance must satisfy before it leaves the research setting.

standards.name: PRoBE (prospective-specimen-collection, retrospective-blinded-evaluation)
standards.applies_to: biomarker study design and specimen provenance

standards.name: TRIPOD+AI
standards.applies_to: reporting of prediction-model development and validation

standards.name: PROBAST+AI
standards.applies_to: risk-of-bias and applicability appraisal of prediction models

claims_contract.consequence_for_this_project: MetaboGuard's current outputs are cross-sectional deviation scores, exploratory phenotypes and reliability audits. They do not meet PRoBE specimen requirements, have no prediagnostic lead time, and are therefore reported as research only.

projected_2050.method: demographic constant-rate projection (population size and ageing only)

disease_burden_projections.approved_wording: Global pancreatic cancer burden was 531,318 cases and 490,786 deaths in 2024, and a demographic constant-rate projection gives 998,663 cases and 936,038 deaths in 2050 if incidence and mortality rates stay unchanged.
denied_wording: Pancreatic cancer cases will double by 2050.
The rise in pancreatic cancer is caused by metabolic disease.
Our model can prevent the projected increase.
disease_burden_projections.note: This is a demographic projection holding rates constant, not a causal forecast and not a prediction of what will happen.
